
> **Python or Rust?** The same model, functions and arguments exist in
> [Python](../../python/index.html) (`m.verb(...)` for R's `verb(m, ...)`)
> and [Rust](../../rust/basemapper_core/index.html). Coming from 0.2? See
> [Migrating to 0.3](../../migrating-to-0.3.html).

basemapper renders MapLibre GL basemaps headlessly with a Rust core: no
browser, display server, GPU or GDAL. Vector styles are drawn by a software
port of MapLibre GL JS's renderer, so maps look as they do in MapLibre.
Everything on this page was run when the page was built; the maps are the
output of the code above them.

## Installation

```r
# Any one of these installs the latest release; each compiles the Rust core.
pak::pak("ar-puuk/basemapper/r-basemapper")
remotes::install_github("ar-puuk/basemapper", subdir = "r-basemapper")
devtools::install_github("ar-puuk/basemapper", subdir = "r-basemapper")
```

## A first map

`basemap()` takes a style and what you know of the map: here a centre and a
zoom, and the image's size. Printed in a document, a basemap shows the map:

```{r}
library(tmap)        # (for the tmap example below) before basemapper,
library(basemapper)  # whose tm_basemap() replaces tmap's

m <- basemap("OpenFreeMap.Positron", center = c(-111.8887, 40.7556), zoom = 12.4, width = 720, height = 405)
m
```

`print()` describes it: each value, and where it came from (*given*, or
*derived* from the others, or a *default*):

```{r}
print(m)
```

The simplest style is a named basemap; `list_providers()` lists them, with
the API key some need. A MapLibre style URL or JSON works too, and so does
tile data (see [Your own tiles and services](own-data.html)).

```{r}
head(list_providers()[, c("name", "vector", "raster", "api_key_env")], 8)
```

## Three controls

A map answers three questions, each with one argument:

| Question | Argument |
|---|---|
| What to show | the extent: `bounds` (an area), or `center` with `zoom` (the camera) |
| How much detail | `zoom`: which roads, places and labels the style draws |
| How sharp | `dpi`: pixels per inch (96 by default) |

`width` / `height` give the image's size, in pixels or (with `units`)
inches, cm or mm. **Any three of extent, zoom, image size and dpi give the
fourth**, and what nothing gives is defaulted: dpi 96, then 800 x 600, then
the world. The zoom is never a default; it is derived. So an area alone gets
the zoom that fits it in 800 x 600:

```{r}
nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
basemap("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", bounds = nc, width = 720, height = 300)
```

An area and a zoom give the image size: *this area at this detail*.

```{r}
detail <- basemap("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", bounds = nc, zoom = 6)
get_size(detail)
```

`around()` gives an area by its size on the ground:

```{r}
basemap("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", bounds = around(c(-111.89, 40.76), c(12, 6), units = "km"),
        width = 720, height = 360)
```

And `dpi` is sharpness: the same map, with more pixels.

```{r}
print_ <- basemap("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", bounds = nc, width = 7, height = 3, units = "in", dpi = 300)
get_size(print_)    # 2100 x 900 pixels: 7 x 3 inches at 300 dpi
```

## Renderings

`render()` draws a basemap once; the rendering converts to a PNG, an array
or a {terra} raster, and knows where it is:

```{r}
img <- render(m)
img
write_png(img, file.path(tempdir(), "slc.png"))
dim(as_array(img))
as_raster(img)
```

`render(m, dpi = 192)` renders the same view at 192 dpi. `m` gives its size
in pixels, so the image keeps them and covers less ground; a basemap with no
size (or one in inches) is the same map with twice the pixels. `render_svg()`
draws an SVG, with the map as paths and the labels as editable text:

```{r}
slc <- c(-111.8910, 40.7608)
raster <- basemap("OpenStreetMap.Mapnik", center = slc, zoom = 11.5, width = 480, height = 300)
vector <- basemap("OpenFreeMap.Bright", center = slc, zoom = 11.5, width = 480, height = 300)

out <- file.path(tempdir(), c("raster.png", "raster.svg", "vector.png", "vector.svg"))
write_png(render(raster), out[1])
render_svg(raster, out[2])
write_png(render(vector), out[3])
render_svg(vector, out[4])
data.frame(file = basename(out), kb = round(file.size(out) / 1024))
```

```{r formats, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
# Show the four files written above.
show <- file.path(knitr::opts_chunk$get("fig.path"), basename(out))
dir.create(dirname(show[1]), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
invisible(file.copy(out, show, overwrite = TRUE))
cat(sprintf(
  '<table class="table" style="table-layout:fixed"><col style="width:7.5em"><col><col><tr><th></th><th>PNG</th><th>SVG</th></tr>
<tr><th>Raster<br><small>OpenStreetMap</small></th><td><img src="%s" style="width:100%%"></td><td><img src="%s" style="width:100%%"></td></tr>
<tr><th>Vector<br><small>OpenFreeMap Bright</small></th><td><img src="%s" style="width:100%%"></td><td><img src="%s" style="width:100%%"></td></tr></table>',
  show[1], show[2], show[3], show[4]
))
```

## Any CRS

A map is drawn in Web Mercator, as every web map, unless it says otherwise:
`crs` gives its CRS, and a spatial layer in a projected CRS gives its own.
The map is then warped into it:

```{r}
nc_lcc <- sf::st_transform(nc, 32119)   # North Carolina's state plane
basemap("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", bounds = nc_lcc, width = 720, height = 300)
```

## In a plot

Add a basemap to a {ggplot2} plot. The plot gives the extent, the CRS, the
size and the dpi; the basemap renders when the plot is drawn, lines up with
the data in any CRS, and credits the provider in the corner:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(nc) +
  basemap("OpenFreeMap.Positron") +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = BIR74 / 1000), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c("Births, 1974\n(thousands)") +
  theme_void()
```

`tm_basemap()` does the same in {tmap} (attach tmap first: it has a
`tm_basemap()` of its own):

```{r, message = FALSE}
tm_basemap("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas") +
  tm_shape(nc) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "SID74", fill_alpha = 0.7, fill.legend = tm_legend("SIDS, 1974"))
```

[Plots with ggplot2 and tmap](plotting.html) has more.

## Clipping

`clip` draws a basemap only inside a layer's polygons; `outside()` draws it
everywhere else. An inside clip also frames the map on the layer:

```{r}
wake <- nc[nc$NAME == "Wake", ]
basemap("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", clip = wake, width = 720, height = 400)
```

## What basemapper tells you

Renders carry notes. A value basemapper chose is shown by `print()`;
something it had to change (the view kept inside the world, an effective
dpi in a plot) is a message, once; something missing from the map (a tile
that failed) is a warning, every time, and an error with
`fetch_options(on_error = "fail")`.

```{r}
img$notes[, c("level", "kind", "message")]
```

## The tile cache

Tiles are cached on disk, so drawing an area again does not download its
tiles again. They are kept for as long as each server allows (a day when it
says nothing), and past 250 MB the least recently used go first.

```{r}
tile_cache()  # where the tiles are kept
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
tile_cache(max_size = 500)       # a 500 MB limit
tile_cache("D:/basemap-tiles")   # another folder, for this session
tile_cache(FALSE)                # no cache, for this session
tile_cache(clear = TRUE)         # delete the cached tiles
```

To keep a folder or limit for good, set them in your `.Renviron`
(`usethis::edit_r_environ()` opens it) and restart R:

```
BASEMAPPER_CACHE_DIR=D:/basemap-tiles
BASEMAPPER_CACHE_MAX_SIZE=500
```

Python reads the same variables, so one folder can serve both languages.
